hook.text: Why does a string play these notes?

text.formula: Tied at both ends: whole loops only
Each loop more: a higher note

youtube.title: Why a string only plays certain notes 🎸 #shorts
youtube.description:
A string tied at both ends can only fit whole half-waves. Harmonic n has n loops, a wavelength of 2L/n and n times the frequency of the first.

text.formula: The wave moves, the beads only bob
Half the wavelength: twice the frequency

youtube.title: Wavelength and frequency in 30 seconds 🌊 #shorts
youtube.description:
Speed = frequency × wavelength. At the same speed, a wave half as long passes twice as often: a higher note. Sound is the same wave, made of squeezed and stretched air.

youtube.title: Circles that draw a square wave 🔵 #shorts
youtube.description:
Each spinning circle is one sine wave. Add them, biggest first, and a square wave appears. Different circle sizes draw a triangle instead.

hook.text: How do musicians tune by ear?

text.formula: 6 and 8 a second: 2 wobbles a second
Same note: no wobble, in tune

youtube.title: How to tune by ear: listen for beats 〰️ #shorts
youtube.description:
Two close notes add up to a sound that swells and fades |f₁ − f₂| times a second. As the notes get closer the wobble slows down; when it stops they are in tune.

youtube.title: What musical intervals look like 🎹 #shorts
youtube.description:
An oscilloscope draws one note against another. Simple ratios draw calm shapes and sound sweet; complicated ratios scribble and sound tense.

hook.text: Why does a siren change pitch?

text.formula: Faster than sound: a shock cone

youtube.title: The Doppler effect, then a sonic boom 🚑 #shorts
youtube.description:
A moving source squeezes its waves in front and stretches them behind, so the pitch is higher ahead and lower behind. Faster than sound, the waves pile into a cone.
